key_insight: RoboTTT shows that robot policies can use extremely long visuomotor context—up to 8K timesteps—without increasing inference latency. This unlocks new abilities like one-shot imitation from human video, online policy improvement, and greater robustness.
problem_solved: Most robot foundation models rely on short history or single-step context, limiting their ability to learn from long demonstrations, adapt during deployment, and use richer temporal information.
method: Introduces Test-Time-Training Robot Policies (RoboTTT), a robot model and training recipe designed to scale context length dramatically.
Uses long-horizon visuomotor context during training and inference while keeping runtime cost effectively unchanged.
Enables test-time adaptation so the policy can improve from context and demonstrations in real time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this expands what robot policies can do with the same inference budget, making long-context adaptation practical for real-world robotics. It also suggests a new path toward more flexible, data-efficient, and robust embodied AI systems.

paper_title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
paper_authors: Yunfan Jiang, Yevgen Chebotar, Ruijie Zheng, Fengyuan Hu, Yunhao Ge
